---
title: "Go-around"
description: "How OPDI finds an approach that was given up and flown again (go-around)."
---

## In one sentence

A `go-around` is an approach that the aircraft gives up before touching down,
climbing away to try again; the event is placed at the lowest point of the
approach.

## What it needs

- The destination airport of the flight list and its elevation.
- The runways of that airport (from OurAirports), for the approach corridor.
- Reports with an altitude near the airport, at most 10 NM from it.

## How it is computed

The detector works on the height of the aircraft above its destination
airport, so it also finds approaches abandoned before the runway.

1. Find each moment the height falls through **500 ft** and each moment it
   rises through **1,500 ft**. A dead band of 50 ft on each side keeps an
   aircraft flying level near one of these heights from giving a series of
   crossings. The moments are interpolated between reports.
2. Pair each rise through 1,500 ft with the last fall through 500 ft before
   it. The time between them is one **excursion**.
3. Keep the excursion when all of these hold:
   - its lowest point is more than 15 ft above the airport, so the aircraft
     did not touch down (15 ft is the height that defines `ALDT`);
   - no report in between is flagged on the ground, and none is slower than
     50 kt without an altitude (a landing roll or a taxi);
   - the aircraft climbs at 500 ft/min or more at some point;
   - the lowest point is at most 10 NM from the airport and lies in the
     approach corridor of one of its runways: at most 5 NM before a threshold
     or over the runway, and at most 0.5 NM from the extended centre line.
     When the airport's runways are not known, this condition is not applied;
   - the excursion lasts at most 600 s, and no two consecutive reports in it
     are more than 60 s apart (a landing followed by a take-off, or a hole in
     the data, is not a go-around).
4. The event is placed at the lowest point of the excursion.

## Based on

- Developed for OPDI: a descent below 500 ft above the airport followed by a
  climb above 1,500 ft, close to a runway.
- Comparable to, but developed separately from, the go-around detection of
  the [`traffic`](../resources.qmd#ref-olive-2019) library (`GoAroundDetection`), which
  looks instead for two approaches aligned with a runway, separated by a
  climb. [Proud (2020)](../resources.qmd#ref-proud-2020) published another method for
  finding go-arounds in ADS-B positions and compared it with earlier ones.
- Study: [Flight events from ADS-B, version 4](../../papers/flight-events-v4/index.html).

## What is published

Event type `go-around`, with position, altitude, `distance_flown_nm` and
`time_passed_s`. Its `info` holds `apt_icao` (destination airport),
`low_height_ft` (lowest height above the airport), `recovery_roc_ft_min`
(highest rate of climb afterwards, in ft/min) and `excursion_seconds` (see
the [Data dictionary](../data/dictionary.qmd#info-fields)).

## Use cases

- **Go-around rate per airport and runway**: go-arounds divided by landings
  (`ALDT`), for example by weather period.
- **Extra time and distance**: `distance_flown_nm` and `time_passed_s` from
  the `go-around` to the final `ALDT` of the same flight.
- **Holding after a missed approach**: combine with `holding-start` later on
  the same flight.

## Limitations

A go-around above 1,500 ft, or one that never descended below 500 ft, is not
found; a training approach flown as a low pass is counted. See
[Limitations: runway events](../limitations.qmd#lim-runway).
